value.text: The town plan of Imola, Windsor RL 12284, autumn 1502

claims.statement: The town plan of Imola, Windsor RL 12284, autumn 1502 (Itinerario tier A)

sources.loc: section Romagna and the Marches in the service of Cesare Borgia, Documentary anchors

background.text: The Imola plan combines pacing with an odometer and bearings taken by compass to render the town as a true plan, an ichnographia seen from directly above: among the earliest measured town plans in existence. A circular frame carries the eight wind names, and marginal notes give the distances to neighboring towns; the drawing marks the passage from the intuitive bird's eye view to the coordinate plan. Its context is the confinement of Cesare at Imola in the autumn of 1502, during the revolt of his captains at Magione. In precisely those months the envoy of the Florentine republic resident at the Borgia court in Imola was Machiavelli, whose dispatches survive (legation of October to December 1502 A ). This is the one interval in which the presence of Leonardo and Machiavelli at the same court can be fixed by documents on both sides; no document records a direct exchange between them D , but the overlap itself is established at tier A.
